numbers.context: PSGN latency after pharyngitis or impetigo

negations.rule: Nephrotic syndrome lacks prominent glomerular inflammation
Nephrotic urinalysis has fatty casts/oval fat bodies without RBC casts

negations.phrase: Do not diagnose nephrotic syndrome on dipstick alone without quantifying proteinuria ≥3.5 g/day
negations.rule: Always quantify proteinuria ≥3.5 g/day before diagnosing nephrotic syndrome
MPGN and diffuse proliferative lupus nephritis can present as mixed nephritic-nephrotic

conditions.rule: Dipstick alone is insufficient without quantification
Renal vein thrombosis risk is highest in membranous nephropathy

highYield.fact: Proteinuria cut-off: nephritic <3.5 g/day vs nephrotic ≥3.5 g/day (UPCR ≥3.5 g/g)
Urine sediment: nephritic = dysmorphic RBCs/acanthocytes + RBC casts; nephrotic = fatty casts + oval fat bodies + Maltese crosses, no RBC casts
Nephritic hallmarks: oliguria, azotaemia, hypertension; prototypes PSGN (2-4 wk, low C3) vs IgA nephropathy (1-3 d, normal C3) vs RPGN (crescents)

Nephrotic hallmarks: hypoalbuminaemia <3.0 g/dL, anasarca, hyperlipidaemia, hypercoagulability (antithrombin III loss → renal vein thrombosis in membranous), encapsulated bacterial infections (Ig loss)
Mnemonic PHARAOH mapped 1:1 to nephritic features
Overlap syndromes: MPGN and diffuse proliferative lupus nephritis can show both nephritic and nephrotic features
